text:
alex: FYI I opened the office fridge and found someone versioned the leftovers with semver. 0.0.1-beta-ketchup 😅
maria: classic. did it pass the compatibility test with the sandwich? :thinking_face:
tim: only if the sandwich uses YAML for condiments. indents matter.
jen: seriously though, pro tip: never put `:` in your lunch label unless you want CI to fail.
ci-bot: build failed for branch lunch-labels — error parsing manifest at line 3: mapping values are not allowed here
alex: lol the fridge is now a broken parser. my label was `mayo:legacy
version: 1.0` (I admit nothing)
maria: that explains the semver prank. you used `1.0` instead of `1.0.0` — the sandwich is in a minor meltdown.
tim: there should be a new RFC: semver-for-foods. must bump patch for extra pickles, minor for new cheese, major for gluten.
jen: vote: should we enforce `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` on lunch labels? React with :thumbsup: for yes, :pizza: for maybe, :shrug: for no
alex: also we need a compiler meme corner: spotted on the fridge — "The compiler told me to go outside. I did. Now it's linking errors."
maria: (adds sticker) +1 for fridge memes.
ci-bot: Reminder: to mute spurious fridge-parse alerts add `skip-lunch-manifest: true` to .ci.yml
tim: someone add that to the repo pls. PR title: "chore: tolerate condiment-legacy formatting"
jen: PR body: "Adds temporary leniency for labels created during hangry hours. Includes tests asserting the sandwich still tastes the same."
maria: acceptance criteria: no YAML crying, no semver therapy sessions between 12-1pm.
alex: closing note: if you find a taco labeled `v2.0.0-alpha+spicy` it's mine. do not touch.
jen: noted. enforced by fridge ACLs. :lock:
